answer: Each proposed identity must complete a challenge-bound chain of sequential modular squarings before it is accepted; a Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check the result efficiently. GPUs can run separate chains in parallel, but cannot skip the dependency between squarings within a chain, so cloning still requires proportionally more compute while each clone faces a physical delay. This bottleneck is a jetty against cheap Sybils, not a signal of unique personhood; a grove of machines can still multiply identities given enough time and hardware.
